reviews.text: 好的游戏，但是有一个影响游戏体验的BUG。 通过输入符号查询图鉴的设定很有意思，但是我在一次错误输入后输入页面出现BUG，我点击各种符号都会发出声音，但是并不能正常输入。 于是我关闭了游戏再进入，结果我解锁了所有的飞船（在之前我第一艘船在困难难度下没坚持多久，只解锁了第二艘船） 现在我拥有所有的船了，但是并不是通过正常的完成波次解锁的。 而且我现在已经解锁了英雄功能，但是我并没有在正式版游戏中通关过（在我之前游玩的体验版中，我通关一次后才解锁英雄） 又或者说我是发现了隐藏好的作弊代码？类似上上下下左左右右BABA的作弊码。 (Machine Translation) Good game, but there is a bug that affects the gaming experience. It's interesting to query the settings of the image guide by inputting symbols, but I encountered a BUG on the input page after a mistake. Clicking on various symbols would make a sound, but I couldn't input them properly. So I closed the game and entered again, and as a result, I unlocked all the ships (my first ship didn't last long in difficult situations before, only unlocking the second ship) Now I have all the ships, but they were not unlocked through normal completion of waves. And I have already unlocked the hero function, but I have not completed it in the official version of the game (in the experience version I played before, I unlocked the hero only after completing it once) Or did I discover the hidden cheating code? Similar to cheat codes for Up UP down down left left right right BABA. 2025.1.29 我想我知道BUG的出现原因了，拿鱼雷艇举例，在测试版游戏中我们可以通过完成回合直接解锁，但是在正式版里我们需要研究，像是“机械巡洋舰”之类的飞艇我仍然需要研究解锁，但是在触发之前的BUG后我解锁了原本测试版中已经获得的全部内容（如测试版本中的所有英雄和鱼雷艇） 我刚刚解锁新的研究发现研究结果中的英雄角色我已经获得了，或许是测试版中的存档被继承到了正式版。

i love ACtS and when i saw that they were making a survivors-type roguelike i thought it had potential with how modular the ship designer was, as well as the creativity in monsters. unfortunately i have to call this one a miss. its just kind of bland, and difficult in a way that does not feel rewarding. when completing the missions i simultaneously feel dissatisfied with what loot i got, and lack a feeling of progress or achievement in overcoming. i feel like the game mimicked a lot of mechanics but did not do so in a way that meshes them together well. the branching map path feels decidedly unsatisfying. instead of less restrictive the shop makes the upgrade options feel more restrictive than take-it-or-leave-it draft picks are. at the core of it though i dislike the gameplay when you are under threat there's not really anything that you can do about it, when you arent under threat there's not really anything to do but fly at whichever arrow pops up and manuever to pick up scrap. enemy spawn patterns suck, and picking up scrap is boring. additionally because the game operates on a time til mission ends model and there arent any "vaccum" powers or abilities it means that if you are under pressure and have to manuever to survive you are losing even if you survive becasue you have been forced away from scrap pickup which means that the hardest fights are the least rewarding. and the scavanger escort has a tiny range, it will sometimes idle while there is even scrap onscreen in the corner. in short, when you are doing well its boring, and when its exiting it is unrewarding, the worst of both worlds. its pretty unforgiving in difficulty, theres no metaprogression, and the ingame progession isnt great. i would rather that it move away from one of: the shop, scrap collection, or level-based battles. the three are not working together, they are fighting each other. and lastly, in ACtS i feel attached to my ship designs, i think "i wanted this ship to do a thing and it does (or fails to do) that thing." i have not felt attached to any design or build in this game, i think that it fundamentally misses the spirit of Airships.

Game that feels like it was made by a mad hatter, the concept looks very interesting, but I have encountered one issue that made me return the game. Unlike games like Brotato, which are challenging but fair, this one just feels like you have to earn the right to get anywhere, instead of the developer actually trying to make the game somewhat accommodating. I've played couple of rounds, some where I got reasonably far, some where I would die relatively quickly. My issue isn't that I get upset if I lose. I would get upset with Brotato all the time, and I think that's a great game with fantastic value. So what gives? Most of the ships use tank controls. Should I even explain how much more difficult it is to try to make a split second decisions with that control scheme? How much harder it is to avoid projectiles? And not just that, you have to collect resources too - anything you miss is lost forever. I've found that I simply don't know how much longer I'll have to play, before I can actually tell if I'm going to have a reasonable fun with the game. Do I have to play 10 hours, before I can see some improvement? Do I need 50 hours to grasp the fundamentals properly? Or will I find in 5 hours that I simply don't find this game too fun, because I'll never 'git gud'? With aforementioned Brotato, the enemies wouldn't be so rabid, and the characters follow your controls well, so when I take damage, most of the time I feel like I've messed up. I would see the challenge and appeal of having so many strong items, which I have to carefully use together or hope to acquire. The genius of that game comes from the many characters, which also serve as sort of a difficult options - here, maybe my mistake was choosing "normal" difficulty, but the combination of very aggressive enemies and clumsy ship controls made me feel like I was playing on very hard the whole time. In Lost Flotilla, you not only struggle due to clumsy controls, but you also feel weak - I can't help but feeling the game is annoying and clunky in this aspect. Avoiding enemy projectiles is so much harder with tank controls, and you also aren't sturdy enough to take too many hits, so you often just end up running away from them. Which causes problems with collecting enough resources. And upgrades mostly felt incremental, some made me excited, but with the exception of expensive weapon upgrades, I wouldn't feel much difference. I don't know how much fun and value this game can provide, because it just makes a poor first impression. It is a shame, because maybe I could have a lot of fun, but I feel like the developer could do it a little better, so that I could see in first 2 hours, how much potential the game really has. Oh, and the UI isn't just bare bones and un-intuitive, it's unfinished - you do not have to be an UX designer to be able to come up with some major improvements. A reward from a mission shouldn't appear as a free item on the market tab, just give it to the player, you have a basic dialogue window, just use that... UI is a tool to convey information. Try to listen out to players, look at playthroughs and see where people struggle to find the information they need. Instead of balancing the game, where you're making it even harder, try listening more to people that aren't your hardcore audience, coming from the success of your previous (and vastly different) game.

A wonderful gameplay loop comprised of if galaga and brotato had a baby, complete with an indulgent occulty steampunk paintjob. Also gives you a bunch of funny little puzzles to solve for its wide array of unlocks. The dynamic of maneuvering your slow-turning ship around to dodge enemies that have to maneuver the same way gives the game a unique feel for its genre. Try the demo!

It doesn't look like much and yet it's one of the most bizarrely addictive autofire roguelites I've ever played. Each of the many, many ships has different stats, gimmicks, and slots to put weapons, escorts, and modules in as well as different captains with even more passives. Making different builds is quite fun and being able to pick what enemies you fight in the node based roguelite path helps you avoid bringing specialized builds to fights you can never win. The upgrade system mid-run is fun, too as it's based on two resources, one of which can be recouped by selling back the stuff you already have to replace with other stuff and the other of which is mostly for buying passive upgrades. The weapons, escorts, and modules themselves can be upgraded to better versions with money and they often have different upgrade paths, too. Lastly, the metaprogression isn't strength based unlike other roguelites so you won't really feel like the difficulty is unbalanced due to its existence. It mostly consists of filling out a bestiary full of lore with some interesting secret codes to find and some of the bestiary entries unlock new ships and captains. The research progresses by you killing the enemy type that's being researched or by "researching in the background" which causes things to be researched in real time (the game gives you a date and time in real life for when the research will finish) so you don't have to fight rare enemies or enemies you simply hate fighting. You might be disappointed coming from Airships: Conquer the Skies but that's a given considering this spinoff is a game in a completely different genre. The lore, vibes, and charm of Airships: CtS are still here and even some of the game design and there's a surprising amount of variety in its gameplay.

I like it. Vampire Survivor-like with lots of guns, bombs, missiles, magic missiles, etc... There is a book full of secret pages that acts as the achievements list for unlocking more ships, captains, and gear. Lots of fun deciphering new pages to find more pages, discovering the last piece of a puzzle spread across four older pages,... It's a great way to get players interested in the lore too. Very clever and versatile feature. The variety of ships is very satisfying. From weapon/gear slots, starting equipment, stats and unique features, the game makes most ships feel special. Hell, even movement is different between them; Some use the typical survivor-like up,down,left,right navigation, others use a forward, turn left/right, some can't stop, a few have extra special elements thrown in, it's a lot of fun. It's been a while since I've enjoyed steampunk but this definitely tapped into some old cog-brain stuff. And, even as a basic BulletHeaven, it's easy to pick up. Would recommend. A few Cons: -it'd be nice to be able to save mid run. Some of us have limited/fragmented/unreliable gaming time in our lives. Even just a 'save & quit' would be enough to meet basic accessibility standards here. -Some stats aren't easy to understand. Once you get it, their wording makes technical sense, but it feels like awkward translation. Like, your rate of fire is determined by your reload speed. Sure, that makes sense, but it's not how I'd have worded it and I doubt most devs would disagree with me. Also, repeat ship upgrade cost, huh? I know what it means now and, I say with confidence, this is a terrible name for a stat in a game that contains upgradable: weapons, npc companions, Slotted equipment, and neat stat boosts. -Some will likely disagree with this, but you can skip earning an unlock by "researching" (click the challenge then wait for realtime hours/days). I don't like this. If a player CBF doing the challenge then they'll just look it up online. You don't have to give us a '"technically you're not cheating"' mechanic to skip stuff.

Pretty good, I'll prefer spaceships, but airships are cool too. Runs pretty light as well. One thing that stands out from other similar games that I like is that it has the airship aesthetic right, but it also actually feels like you're flying an airship around, i.e. it has turn rate and your ship actually takes time to turn. So far it isn't really an issue, but I heard there are some ships I haven't yet unlocked that are really sluggish and it's something you have to take into account. As is, so far for me, the main advantage is you can actually feel the difference between a fast small gunboat and a big heavy battleship. There are also some omindirectional movement ships/copters too where it just moves near instantly. Oh and there are also planes where you cannot stop and have to keep flying, so that's pretty cool. It makes it all feel real. Side note, using mouse movement lets you play the whole game just using the mouse, the ship goes towards your cursor, what that also means is that if you want to stop, the keyboard commands don't work, instead put your cursor above your ship and it'll stop. Also opening menu/pause is left click. It's actually pretty sweet that you can run the whole game just using your mouse. Most others would still go with esc only for opening the menu. Weapon selection is pretty nice too, with a wide variety, and then you can upgrade most weapons into two distinct paths. Like the Guided Missile, one of my favorites. It can go into Swarm Missiles that trades range and damage for sheer volume of fire, or Thermobaric Missile which increases it's AOE and sets things on fire. You then also have module slots which allows you to further customize your ship, sometimes even giving them some new capabilities. Like iirc the Alchemy or something module that at base just increases the potency of your explosive weapons, but can be upgraded where now your exploding/AOE weapons now also stuns or fears your enemies. Then there are escorts, mostly not that sexy honestly, but if you want to play a minion class, these are for you. There are some interesting stuff there though, like if you don't have the module slots for shield generators, you can pickup a shield ship instead that does similar while providing other bonuses. Though it also depends, some escorts stick right next to you, these aren't that nice it feels, but there are also those which just roams out to kill, they are like long range weapons. Useful depending on enemies, like when there are those you want to stay away from. Those above are basically slot limited depending on your airship, but there are also passives you can pickup, these are unlimited, though they get more costly as you start stacking them. Mostly they are either just pure stat upgrades or stat tradeoffs, but here there too are interesting stuff, like iirc there is one where you apply an effect, iirc fire, then it also applies another effect, iirc stun. Basically lets you start stacking effects on enemies. There is also an Air Manual thing, i.e. the bestiary among other things, it provides lore, and also stats of enemies. And the interesting part here is that to unlock pages, you can either find the relevant things in game, or enter a code if you can acquire it from somewhere, perhaps from the Steam Guide section. Many of these pages would then have a challenge you must complete in order to unlock new stuff for your runs, basically everything, from ships, captains, to all the stuff you can pickup in a run. And another interesting thing here is you can set them to do research too, i.e. leave it running offline and when it completes the challenge is just marked as complete. This means if there are any annoying challenges that just doesn't fit your playstyle, heavily relies on RNG or otherwise you just don't want to do, you can still slowly unlock them anyway. Though I dunno why they do not have a glossary, like it doesn't explain what fear or armor does exactly for example, you can kinda figure it out just from the name, but it doesn't give you the details. And the map is also annoying to look at because you cannot just scroll/pan, you can actually see the whole map, just click the nodes and it recenters, but it is more annoying compared to just panning it. Also you cannot save mid-run, a run takes around 20 minutes, 60 seconds per node iirc and 20 nodes. Though you can pause, even mid-combat, and the game does run light enough that you can just leave it in the background. So it's more a minor annoyance than anything.

Awesome game, love the art, and love the gameplay loop. Repetitive? Very. Highly rewarding? Yes. All airships have different forms of movement, so you have to adjust to this alongside creating a build that mitigates weaknesses and maximizes strengths. Captains also shift this into different builds. I like that you have to make calculated decisions when picking a path too. Is money more useful to you, or scrap, or the reputation for rewards, or maybe unlocking stuff by murdering flying jelly fish? It's very good, and a great example of READABILITY in visuals. I can see what's happening at all times, and it's very pretty overall with its minimalistic, steampunk design. Just overall a great game. I give most games a thumbs up but this one gets a real thumbs up, like double ice cream thumbs up with a sprinkle of chocolate.
